translationRepairs: In 1736, when the Qianlong Emperor took the throne, Chao reported that flood-hit districts had not technically qualified as disaster areas. The emperor replied: 'Even if the floods have not risen to the level of a declared disaster, you must still relieve the people with special care and keep the poor from losing their livelihoods.'

In 1735, when the Qianlong Emperor took the throne, Chao reported that flood-hit districts had not technically qualified as disaster areas. The emperor replied: 'Even if the floods have not risen to the level of a declared disaster, you must still relieve the people with special care and keep the poor from losing their livelihoods.'
Preceding units date Yongzheng 十一/十二年 as 1733/1734, so 十三年 is AD 1735; s0016's 乾隆元年 is 1736. Gaozong's accession in 雍正十三年 is 1735, not 1736.
After Yinpei was transferred to Fujian, Governor Chang Jun protected Hongsui. Qilang cried injustice and impeached Zhaolin, who memorialized in turn.
After Yinpei was transferred to Fujian, Governor Chang Jun shielded Hongsui and impeached Zhaolin, citing Qilang's cry of injustice. Zhaolin also memorialized the throne.
After 巡撫常鈞庇宏燧, 以七郎呼冤劾兆麟 takes Chang Jun as the subject of 劾, with Qilang's cry of injustice as the pretext; the original wrongly makes Qilang the impeacher.
In 1789, blaming slack Fujian governance on him, Jingsu was punished retroactively and exiled to Ili.
In 1789, citing slack Fujian governance, the emperor held the late Jingsu accountable and exiled his son Zhao to Ili.

追咎景素 is posthumous blame of Jingsu; the exile verb 戍 applies to his son 炤 (Zhao), named in s0192. Wikisource/editions read 戍炤 (chapter 戍召 is a graphic garble of 炤), so the original wrongly exiles the already-dead Jingsu.
In 1794 he was released and allowed to return.
In 1794 Zhao was released and allowed to return.
釋回 has no new subject; it continues from the person exiled in s0193, i.e. Zhao (炤), not the dead Jingsu. Naming Zhao removes the false antecedent.
